title: Assessment of LDL cholesterol status and postoperative outcomes in vascular surgery patients: A single-center prospective observational study
summary:
Elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels are a major risk factor for atherosclerotic vascular disease and may influence postoperative outcomes in vascular surgery patients. Despite guideline recommendations, lipid control in this population remains suboptimal.
The aim of this prospective, single-center observational study is to assess the lipid status of patients undergoing vascular surgical treatment and to evaluate its association with postoperative outcomes, including complications, reinterventions, rehospitalizations, and mortality.
Data are collected at baseline during hospital admission, including lipid parameters, medication, and clinical characteristics. Patients are followed for a period of 12 months after the surgical intervention to assess postoperative outcomes. All data are derived from routine clinical care, medical records, and standardized questionnaires, without additional interventions.
conditions: Investigation of lipid status and its association with postoperative outcomes in patients with peripheral arterial disease, carotid artery stenosis, or aortic pathologies undergoing vascular surgical treatment, including assessment of the achievement of guideline-recommended LDL cholesterol target levels.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Hospitalized patients undergoing vascular surgical care (conservative, interventional, or surgical treatment)
Ability to provide informed consent
Sufficient understanding of the German language to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
Inability to provide informed consent (e.g., due to language barriers or impaired capacity)
Emergency treatment situation
